newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia oil up on futures, traders play Brent/Dubai.
newsitem.headline: Asia oil up on futures, traders play Brent/Dubai.

text.p: Traders faced listless trade in early Asia cash crude markets on Tuesday, but a flurry of deals on the Brent/Dubai spread suggested widespread hedging on purchases of West African grades, traders said.
In a motionless market, notional cash Brent values for August hovered at the $17.85/17.95, up 10 cents from Monday.
The move was in line with Western market gains arising from perceived Iraqi export delays and a mild wave of technical short covering.

While predictions of a neutral API tally for U.S. inventories to be announced later on Tuesday offered little direction, Iraq's continued balking on the resumption of its exports kept futures markets buzzing.
July WTI on the ACCESS after-hours system rose 13 cents from Monday's New York settlement, to $19.14 as of 0315 GMT.

Asia continued to focus on possible West African deliveries in August, with one August Brent/Dubai sold at plus 77 cents by a Wall Street trader to a U.S. trader, and another said done at plus 80 cents from a separate Wall Street trader to a different U.S. trader.
A September Brent/Dubai was heard switching hands at plus 95 cents from a U.S. trader to a European major, traders said.
"People are out there balancing their books in line with their West African deals," said one Japanese trader.
Separately, the IOC issued its monthly crude tender to cover one million barrels of its August spot needs.
Traders said the tender closes on June 25 at 0000 GMT, with offers valid until 1630 GMT on June 26.
